articles.title: Volunteers Turn Out for the Spring Cleanup Across Lower Millrace
articles.deck: Residents of Lower Millrace filled the hall on Thursday to ask questions about the plan.
body: Rosalind Iwasaki, who has lived in Lower Millrace for 5 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Thursday mornings.

articles.title: Irene Dunmore, 68, Parish Bookkeeper
articles.deck: Friends remember Irene Dunmore for the many years of service to Upper Commons.
body: Born in Upper Commons in the years after the war, Irene Dunmore spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.
Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Upper Commons.

articles.title: Council Approves $18,500 for Carver Avenue Repairs
articles.deck: The vote came after 34 residents spoke at Sunday’s session.
body: Public works estimates the work will take about 34 weeks once it starts in July. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Residents of Cedar Hollow said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

articles.title: Upper Commons Garden Club Adds Footpath Repair
articles.deck: Residents of Upper Commons met on Wednesday to talk over the plan.
body: Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Kettle Hill Park gate on Wednesday at 7 p.m. Several residents on Juniper Avenue said they had been waiting since 1990 for something like this.
The group has raised $1,200 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

articles.title: Millrace Middle School Adds Seasonal Farmers Market to Fall Schedule
articles.deck: The program begins in August and is open to all students in grade 6 and up.
body: Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for August.
The board will review the results at the end of the fall term. Principal Celia Iwasaki said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers.
